steps.name: Load, QC, and align counts to metadata
steps.question: Do the 121 sample columns in counts.csv align 1:1 with the 120 rows of metadata.csv (case vs control), are there any duplicate/malformed columns (e.g., a stray gene-id column), and are library sizes and sample clustering (PCA on variance-stabilized counts) consistent with a single batch with no outliers?
acceptance_criteria: Reports the exact resolution of the 121-vs-120 column/row mismatch (e.g., first column is gene symbol, leaving 120 sample columns matching metadata rows)
Reports per-sample library size (total counts) and number of genes with zero counts across all samples
Produces a PCA or MDS plot of variance-stabilized counts colored by case/control status, flags any sample as an outlier by >3SD on PC1/PC2 or by extreme library size
Final aligned count matrix and metadata table are written for downstream steps, with any excluded or flagged samples explicitly listed and justified

steps.name: DESeq2 differential expression: cases vs controls
steps.question: Which of the ~12000 whole-blood genes are differentially expressed between the 60 cases and 60 controls, using DESeq2's negative-binomial Wald test on raw counts with independent filtering and Benjamini-Hochberg FDR correction?
acceptance_criteria: DESeq2 dataset built from raw integer counts and the aligned metadata with condition (case/control) as the sole design factor (unpaired, single batch, so no covariate adjustment beyond condition unless T1S1 flags confounding)
Independent filtering enabled (default DESeq2 behavior) and Benjamini-Hochberg FDR (padj) reported for every tested gene
Full results table (gene, baseMean, raw log2FC, lfcSE, stat, pvalue, padj) written for all ~12000 genes
Number of genes with padj < 0.05 reported explicitly as a headline statistical-significance count

steps.name: Effect-size shrinkage and large-effect triage
steps.question: After shrinking log2 fold-changes with apeglm (or ashr as fallback) to remove noise-driven inflation at low counts, which of the FDR-significant genes also show a biologically large effect (e.g., |shrunken log2FC| >= 1, i.e., >=2-fold change) versus which are significant but small in magnitude?
acceptance_criteria: apeglm (coefficient-based) shrinkage applied to the case-vs-control contrast from T1S2; if apeglm fails on the contrast parameterization, ashr is used and the fallback is stated

Every gene classified into one of: not significant; significant but small effect (padj<0.05, |shrunken log2FC|<1); significant and large effect (padj<0.05, |shrunken log2FC|>=1) — thresholds stated explicitly and justified as conventional, not tuned post hoc
Counts reported for each of the three categories
Volcano plot (shrunken log2FC vs -log10 padj) and MA plot produced, with the large-effect significant genes labeled
Ranked table of the large-effect significant genes (sorted by |shrunken log2FC|) written as the primary deliverable of this track

steps.name: Pathway enrichment of large-effect DE genes
steps.question: Are the genes classified as significant-and-large-effect (from T1S3) enriched for specific biological pathways or processes, using human hallmark, GO Biological Process, Reactome, and WikiPathways gene sets, relative to significant-but-small-effect genes as a contrast?
acceptance_criteria: Over-representation analysis (or fgsea rank-based test on the full shrunken-log2FC-ranked gene list as a complementary approach) run against MSigDB human hallmark gene sets, MSigDB human GO-BP gene sets, Reactome human pathways, and WikiPathways human pathways (all confirmed present in the reference store)
Background/universe for ORA is the full set of ~12000 tested genes from T1S2, not a generic genome-wide background
BH-adjusted enrichment p-values reported; top pathways (padj<0.05) listed per gene-set collection

Results explicitly note whether large-effect genes enrich for pathways distinct from the small-effect-only significant genes, to test whether effect-size triage is picking out a coherent biological signal versus noise

steps.name: Immune cell composition deconvolution as a confound check
steps.question: Given whole-blood tissue, does estimated immune cell-type composition (e.g., neutrophil, lymphocyte, monocyte proportions) differ between the 60 cases and 60 controls, and does this compositional shift plausibly explain part of the large-effect gene set identified in T1S3 (e.g., large-effect genes that are canonical markers of a shifted cell type)?
acceptance_criteria: Immune cell-type proportions estimated per sample from the normalized bulk count matrix using an available deconvolution method (e.g., xCell or another method from immunedeconv appropriate for whole blood without requiring a paid/gated signature matrix)
Case vs control comparison of estimated proportions per cell type (Wilcoxon or t-test, BH-corrected)

Cross-reference: for each large-effect significant gene from T1S3, flag whether it is a canonical marker gene of a cell type found to be significantly shifted in proportion, explicitly reported as a potential compositional confound rather than a per-cell regulatory change
Caveat stated that bulk deconvolution estimates are indirect and this is a confound-flagging exercise, not a cell-type-resolved DE analysis

plan.title: Whole-blood DE (60 cases vs 60 controls) with effect-size triage
plan.analytical_narrative: The data is a single-batch bulk RNA-seq raw count matrix (12000 genes x 121 samples, one sample column is presumably a gene-symbol/ID artifact to be confirmed against the 120-row metadata) from whole blood, 60 cases vs 60 controls, unpaired. The research question explicitly separates statistical significance from effect-size magnitude ('not only significant'), so the plan is built around three tracks: (1) a rigorous DESeq2 differential expression analysis with proper size-factor normalization, independent filtering, and effect-size shrinkage (apeglm/ashr) so that log2FC estimates used for effect-size triage are not inflated by noise in low-count genes; (2) explicit large-effect triage combining significance (FDR) with shrunken log2FC magnitude thresholds and visualization (volcano, MA plot) to separate 'significant but small' from 'significant and large'; (3) functional interpretation of the large-effect gene set via pathway enrichment (hallmark, GO-BP, Reactome, WikiPathways human gene sets, all present in the reference store) and, because the tissue is whole blood, an immune-cell-composition deconvolution step to check whether the top DE signal is actually a compositional shift in immune cell proportions (a common and often-overlooked confound in blood transcriptomics) rather than a per-cell regulatory change. QC steps (library size, PCA, sample-swap check against metadata) precede DE testing since single-batch design still needs confirmation of no gross outliers/mislabeling before trusting effect sizes.
